syllabus_index.title: Contribution from different parts of country

entries.question: The arts of Indus valley were free from religious influences both aesthetically and functionally. Analyse.
The evolution of various styles of pottery in India from the Indus Valley Civilisation to the later Vedic period was intricately linked with the socio-cultural life of the people. Discuss.
The various archaeological evidences paint a rich picture of the social, economic and religious life of the Harappan people. Discuss.
The various archaeological evidences paint a rich picture of the social, economic and religious life of the Harappan people. Discuss.
How did the enduring legacy of the Harappan Civilization leave a mark on the evolution of Indian culture, even after its sudden decline?
The cave paintings epitomize the artistry and grandeur of the Indian classical painting tradition. Comment.
Bring out the evolution of mural traditions in South India. Also, elaborate on their significant characteristics.
With examples, discuss how the cultural traditions from various regions of India get reflected in regional music.

Indian classical dances not just represent episodes from mythology but also showcase divine and spiritual aspects of life. In this context, explain how are classical dances different from folk dances.
The traditional theatre forms of India reflect the ideals and emotions of the society, and an individual's role in the community. Discuss with examples.
With the elephant being a vital part of the Buddhist faith, it was widely represented in its sculptures as well. Discuss.
Examine the role of numismatic evidence in understanding the political and economic history of ancient India. Provide specific examples.
How does tribal art provide valuable insights into the cultural perspectives and values of Indian tribal communities?
While most of the early literary traditions were religious writings in some form or the other, Sangam Literature did not follow the same trend. Discuss.
In the context of Indian subcontinent, Sanskrit is perhaps the only language that transcended not only academic disciplines but also the barriers of regions and boundaries. Elaborate.
Sanskrit literature in general and particularly in the Guptan age set a high watermark for the literary history of ancient India. Discuss.
The advent of Buddhism and Jainism was instrumental in the development of architecture in ancient India. Discuss.
Provide an account of the historical and architectural importance of the Sanchi Stupa. Also, discuss how it inspired the future architecture in India.
The Gupta sculptures not only remained models of Indian art for all time to come but also served as ideals for sculptures in regions beyond the boundaries of present day India. Substantiate.
Trace the evolution of Nagara style of temple architecture with suitable examples.
The Cholas are inextricably linked with the zenith of Dravidian art and architecture. Comment.
A major phase in temple architecture in India is associated with the Hoysala style of temple architecture. Discuss.
Variations in temple architecture are reflections of geographical conditions, prevalent economic system and philosophical tradition of the time. Elaborate.
Discuss with examples the key features of Vijayanagara architecture. How did Indo-Islamic elements manifest in their structures?
The advent of Buddhism and Jainism was instrumental in the development of architecture in ancient India. Discuss.
How did the competitive and hostile dynamic between Brahminism and Buddhism over funding, followers, and ideology mark the decline of Buddhism?
How will you explain the different fates of Buddhism and Jainism despite a slew of similarities in the two religions?
The fabric of Indian philosophical thought owes as much to Northern India as to Southern India. Elucidate.

The contributions of Bhakti movement towards the development of a body of devotional literature in vernacular languages is as significant as its liberal social-religious teachings that had a moderating influence on medieval history. Discuss.
Examine the impact of the Sramana tradition on the Vedic religion and its relation with the emergence of Jainism, Buddhism and Ajivika sects.

Explain why Sufism, a liberal reform movement in Islam could deepen its roots in the Indian sub-continent, despite Islam being a foreign religion? Also, bring out the impacts of Sufism on Indian society.
European travellers' accounts in the medieval period have played an important role in shaping our understanding of the empires and people of that period in India. Comment.
The accounts of foreign travellers are seminal in reconstructing the history of ancient India. However, these accounts are not without their limitations. Elucidate.
Numerous foreign travellers have vividly documented their observations of the Vijayanagara Empire over time, offering valuable sources for reconstructing its history. Elucidate.
Bring out the role played by the Ahom Kingdom in shaping the cultural and historical identity of North-East India, and discuss its legacy in contemporary times.
Why did Indian rulers fail to defend their kingdoms against foreign invaders during early medieval period?

Compare and contrast the features of ancient Indian universities like Nalanda and Takshashila with modern state-funded universities in India. What lessons can modern universities learn from ancient ones to improve their effectiveness?
Trade was not just an economic activity in ancient India, it facilitated exchange of ideas and technologies that had social, cultural and political consequences. Discuss.
Trade was not just an economic activity in ancient India, it facilitated exchange of ideas and technologies that had social, cultural and political consequences. Discuss.
The process of consolidation of Bengal, which started after the Battle of Plassey culminated in the Battle of Buxar. Do you think the Battle of Buxar was more important for the British than Plassey?
The British victory in the Battle of Plassey in 1757 not just changed the course of Indian history but also that of the world. Discuss.
Giving a brief overview of the three Carnatic wars, discuss the factors that led to the success of the British over the French in the struggle for control over India.
India was forced into numerous wars post Independence. Highlight the causes and impact of the Indo-Pak and Indo-China wars on our bilateral relationships.
The reactionary policies of Lord Lytton and the liberal policies of his successor Lord Rippon acted as catalyst in the formation of the Indian National Congress. Discuss.
The viceroyalty of Lord Lytton and Lord Ripon was marked by the full display of colonial relation between India and Britain. Elucidate.
The reactionary policies of Lord Lytton and the liberal policies of his successor Lord Rippon acted as catalyst in the formation of the Indian National Congress. Discuss.
Dadabhai Naoroji left an indelible imprint on the national movement. Explain.
Dadabhai Naoroji left an indelible imprint on the national movement. Explain.
Compare and contrast the approach of Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru towards the Indian freedom struggle.
The essence of Gandhiji's constructive programme went well beyond the anti-imperialist nationalist struggle. Comment.
Although Mahatma Gandhi accepted Jawahar Lal Nehru as his successor, the two had marked differences during the freedom struggle and in their vision for independent India. Elaborate.
Do you agree with the view that Gandhian politics was, in a sense, a continuation of Tilak's politics?
Gandhiji changed his methods of struggle against the British from time-to-time to suit the varied circumstances and problems that needed to be tackled. Analyse.
Shed light on the use of symbols and traditions by Mahatma Gandhi for both, integrating masses into national struggle and against social evils.
Bring out the key principles underlying Rabindranath Tagore's vision of nationalism during the Indian freedom struggle.
Bhagat Singh made a real breakthrough in terms of revolutionary ideology, the goals of revolution and forms of revolutionary struggle. Elucidate.
Analyze the ideological differences and similarities between the revolutionary movement(1920-1930s) and the Gandhian non-violent struggle. How did these two ideologies influence each other?
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was instrumental in creating a national consciousness and giving political voice to the masses during the course of national movement. Discuss.

How did Mahatma Gandhi's participation in the Khilafat Movement illustrate his ability to connect diverse issues and mobilize different communities towards a common cause? To what extent did the Khilafat movement achieve its objective?
Non-Cooperation Movement democratized India's freedom struggle but suffered from inherent limitations. Discuss.
In the context of Indian freedom struggle, a discernible trend was seen where large national level movements were usually succeeded with period of revolutionary activities. Comment.
Explain the meaning of the terms Swaraj and Purna Swaraj during the anti-colonial national movement in India. Also, trace the progression of the Indian National Congress in this context.
The 1929 Lahore session of Congress shaped the vision for an independent India in many important ways. Explain.

Individual Satyagraha was not only a well thought out strategy by Mahatma Gandhi given the social and political conditions of that time, but it also set the stage for the Quit India Movement. Comment.

The independence of India was not a result of a forced expulsion of the Empire, as desired by the Quit India Movement; it was rather a confluence of domestic politics and global circumstances. Analyze.
The Quit India movement marked a new direction in the struggle against the British colonial rule in India. Analyse.
Among the major legacies of the Indian freedom movement, civil liberties formed an important one. Analyse.
Growth of the Indian National Movement was both a response to and a reason for changes in the British policy in the country. Elaborate.
The Indian national movement went beyond being a struggle for political power; it encompassed social regeneration and constructive programmes under its ambit. Comment.
Indian national movement was not only a domestic affair of the Indian subcontinent, rather it had an international affair that extended beyond her shores. Elaborate.
It can be argued that the peasant movements of the 20th century, when compared to those in the 19th century, were more organised and nationalistic in nature. Comment.
What were the prominent causes behind the recurring tribal movements in the 19th century? Also, discuss the limitations of these movements.

entries.question: The capitalist class generally remained ambivalent in their support to the Indian National Congress until 1940s. In this context, analyse the varying positions of the Indian capitalists throughout the national movement.

entries.topic_name: Contribution from different parts of country
entries.question: Discuss the role played by the Indian diaspora in the freedom struggle of India, especially during the first half of the 20th century.

entries.topic_name: Contribution from different parts of country
entries.question: Trace the evolution of the press in India. Also, discuss the instrumental impact it had during various stages of the Indian freedom struggle despite the repressive policies of the British.

entries.topic_name: Contribution from different parts of country
entries.question: Highlighting the emergence of the working class movement, discuss its contribution towards India's freedom struggle.

entries.question: India's war of independence was won by the efforts and sacrifices of different sections of the society. In this context, discuss the contributions made by tribal women in the national freedom struggle.
Indian nationalism that confronted British imperialism in the 19th century was a product of colonial modernity. Do you agree?
The combination of internal pulls coupled with external pressure as well as colonial resistance prompted the European powers to relinquish their claim over colonies. Elaborate.
The Indian society's impulse for social change and reform was a response to its opposition to colonial rule. Examine.
Critically analyse the efficacy of linguistic reorganisation of states in addressing the reasons for linguistic divides in post-independent India.
Though the socio-political complexities of the Indian subcontinent may have made partition inevitable, it was the failure of British leadership that led to a bloodbath. Discuss.
Why was it more difficult to rehabilitate refugees in West Bengal as compared to Punjab after partition?
How did the policy of non-alignment reflect the aspirations of India and other newly independent nations to maintain their sovereignty and resist colonial pressures?
How did the policy of non-alignment reflect the aspirations of India and other newly independent nations to maintain their sovereignty and resist colonial pressures?
Despite high hopes associated with it, the Shimla Agreement, 1972 failed to deliver on its initial promises. Examine.
The White Revolution was most successful in the Western part of India. Discuss the factors for this regional success of the White Revolution.
The Simla Agreement (1972) and Lahore Declaration (1999) are two key milestones in the history of the Indian subcontinent. Discuss.

Operation flood gave credence to Gandhian ideas of production by masses and village swaraj, with far reaching impact for post independent India. Discuss the statement and highlight various reasons for success of operation flood.
Although the industrial revolution in every country was different, it produced similar end results wherever it happened. Elucidate.
Bring out the relationship between the industrial revolution and the advent of imperialism in different parts of the world.
Napoleon was the child of French revolution who betrayed the revolution in France but revolutionized other parts of the world. Discuss.
The seeds of distrust planted between the West and Russia during the Bolshevik revolution, manifested in the form of cold war that altered the global order. Discuss.
What are the factors that led to the Russian revolution and what are the consequences of this revolution? Discuss its influence on the Indian national movement.
Iranian revolution, 1979 was unique both in terms of its causes and consequences. Elaborate.
Ideas of social justice, collectivism, and equality defined the socialist movements in 19th century Europe, but their impact was restricted due to several reasons. Comment.
World War I was believed to be a 'war to end all wars'; however, its aftermath made another world war inevitable. Examine.
Describing the Congress attitude towards the Second World War, discuss the failure of the Cripps Mission and its consequences.
The end of World War II marked the birth of a new international order. Examine.
The end of World War II marked the birth of a new international order. Examine.
Cold war started after the second world war; however, its seed were sown right after the Russian Revolution 1917. Do you agree?
What are the circumstances that led to the disintegration of the USSR and the end of the Cold War? How did the end of the cold war contribute to the spread of Globalization across the world?
Collapse of the USSR was as much a consequence of internal unrest as of external factors. Analyze this statement and discuss the impacts of fall of USSR.
Highlight the factors that led the unification of Germany and Italy. To what extent was the unification process similar in the two countries?
Arab-Israel conflict is as much a result of their internal contradictions as an outcome of manipulative tactics of the imperial powers. Explain.
What are the key factors that accelerated decolonization post-World War II?
Why were Asian and African countries so easily dominated and colonized by the western powers? Also, contrast the consequence of this domination for colonizers and colonized countries.
Enumerate the reasons behind outbreak of the civil war in China. Also, analyse the wide-reaching impacts of its outcome.
Mention the changes in atmospheric composition since industrial revolution and their multifaceted repercussions.

Created to protect the future generations from the scourge of war, United Nations (UN) was envisioned to bridge the shortcomings of League of Nations (LoN). In light of the statement, make a comparative analysis of the two bodies.
Bringing out the factors that led to the Meiji restoration, discuss its significance for Japan.
Do you agree with the view that continental blockade was an ill-conceived strategy by Napoleon to conquer Britain through economic means?
